Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The 'heart and soul' was Article 32, not Article 17, which abolishes untouchability.

s: During the debates on its making, the Indian Constitution was criticised as a copy of which Act?
x: Critics called it a 'copy of the Government of India Act, 1935' and a 'lawyers' paradise'.

s: From whom did Ambedkar borrow the term 'constitutional morality'?
x: Ambedkar took the term from George Grote and said constitutional morality has to be cultivated.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched regarding Ambedkar's view of Indian federalism?
o: System – unitary or federal as times require
Centre – strong, to protect weaker sections
States – right to secede from the Union
x: Ambedkar held the Union indestructible, so States have no right to secede; the other pairs reflect his views.

s: In Ambedkar's view, what did India being a 'Union of States' mean?
o: States could secede by a referendum
The Union is indestructible and states have no right to secede
States are sovereign units that formed a compact
The Centre can be dissolved by the states
x: Ambedkar said the Union is indestructible and the states have no right to secede.

s: On which date did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar deliver his final speech in the Constituent Assembly?
x: Ambedkar delivered his final speech in the Constituent Assembly on 25 November 1949.

s: Which of the following was NOT one of the three warnings given by Ambedkar in his final Constituent Assembly speech?
o: Turn political democracy into social democracy.
Abolish the parliamentary system in favour of a presidential system.
Give up the bloody methods of revolution and civil disobedience.
Do not lay liberties at the feet of a great man.
x: Ambedkar warned against violent and extra-constitutional methods, hero-worship in politics, and the failure to establish social democracy. He did not call for abolishing the parliamentary system.

s: Ambedkar's reference to India entering 'a life of contradictions' on 26 January 1950 pointed to the coexistence of which of the following?
o: Federalism with the right of secession
Political equality with social and economic inequality
x: The contradiction lay in political equality coexisting with inequality in social and economic life. Ambedkar urged that political democracy be transformed into social democracy.

s: In his final speech, what did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar call civil disobedience, non-cooperation and satyagraha?
x: He said these methods were now the 'grammar of anarchy' and should be given up.

s: According to Ambedkar, what does bhakti or hero-worship in politics lead to?
x: His second warning: bhakti or hero-worship in politics leads to dictatorship.

s: In his final speech of 25 November 1949, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar said political democracy cannot last unless there lies at its base:
x: Ambedkar said political democracy cannot last unless social and economic democracy lies at its base.

s: Who was elected President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946?
x: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected President on 11 December 1946; Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee.

s: Who was the Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly?
x: B.N. Rau was Constitutional Adviser and prepared the initial draft in October 1947.

s: Who were the two Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly?
x: H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari were Vice-Presidents; T.T. Krishnamachari was a Drafting Committee member.

s: The Draft Constitution, published in February 1948, contained how many Articles?
x: The Draft Constitution was published on 21 February 1948 and contained 315 Articles.

s: On which date was the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly set up?
x: It was set up on 29 August 1947 with seven members, including chairman Ambedkar; Nehru was not a member.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
o: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar — Co-author of the Munshi-Ayyangar language formula
Syed Mohammad Saadullah — Representative from Bombay
N. Madhava Rao — Original member in place of B.L. Mitter
T.T. Krishnamachari — Replaced Dr. K.M. Munshi
x: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar was associated with the Munshi-Ayyangar language formula. Saadullah was from Assam, Madhava Rao replaced B.L. Mitter, and T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan.

s: Who was originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee?
x: K.M. Munshi, who also chaired the Order of Business Committee, was originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee.

s: On which date was the Munshi-Ayyangar formula on the language of the Constitution adopted?
x: The Munshi-Ayyangar formula was adopted on 14 September 1949. The date is also associated with the observance of Hindi Diwas on 14 September.

s: Apart from its chairman, how many other members did the Drafting Committee have?
x: The Drafting Committee had 7 members: the chairman plus 6 others.

s: For how many days did the Drafting Committee sit?
x: The Drafting Committee sat for 141 days.

s: Whom did T.T. Krishnamachari replace in the Drafting Committee?
x: T.T. Krishnamachari replaced D.P. Khaitan (died 1948); N. Madhava Rao replaced B.L. Mitter.

s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee?
x: Nehru was not a member of the Drafting Committee; the other three were.

s: On which date was the Draft Constitution prepared by the Drafting Committee published?
x: The Draft Constitution was published on 21 February 1948 with 315 Articles and 8 Schedules.

s: Which member of the Drafting Committee chaired the Order of Business Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
x: K.M. Munshi, originally the only Congress member of the Drafting Committee, chaired the Order of Business Committee.

s: From where was Dr. B.R. Ambedkar elected to the Constituent Assembly before Partition?
x: Before Partition, Ambedkar was elected from Bengal's Jessore-Khulna area with the support of Jogendra Nath Mandal.

s: After Partition, in whose vacated seat was Dr. B.R. Ambedkar re-elected to the Constituent Assembly from the Bombay Presidency?
x: His Bengal seat went to East Pakistan, so he was re-elected from Bombay in the seat vacated by M.R. Jayakar.

s: The stalling of which Bill made Dr. B.R. Ambedkar resign as Law Minister in September 1951?
x: The omnibus Hindu Code Bill stalled in Parliament and Ambedkar resigned in September 1951.

s: Which law, passed in 1955 as part of the Hindu Code, introduced monogamy and divorce?
x: The Hindu Marriage Act 1955 brought monogamy and divorce; the Hindu Succession Act 1956 made daughters Class I heirs.

s:
Consider the following statements about the Hindu Code Bill:
1. It aimed at monogamy, divorce and inheritance rights of daughters and widows.
2. It was passed as one omnibus bill in 1951.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the omnibus bill stalled and was later passed in parts in 1955-56.

s: In which year were daughters given equal coparcenary rights by an amendment to the Hindu Succession Act?
x: The 2005 amendment to the Hindu Succession Act gave daughters equal coparcenary rights.

s: Which Act of 1956, part of the Hindu Code, made daughters Class I heirs?
x: The Hindu Succession Act, 1956 made daughters Class I heirs; the 2005 amendment gave them equal coparcenary rights.

s: Which post held by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar earned him the title 'Father of the Indian Constitution'?
x: He is the Father / Chief Architect of the Constitution as Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

s: Which title was given to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the law-giver of modern India?
x: Ambedkar is called the 'Modern Manu', the law-giver of modern India.

s:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's declaration that, though born a Hindu, he would not die a Hindu:
1. It was made at Yeola on 13 October 1935.
2. It was made at the Depressed Classes Conference.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Ambedkar made this declaration at the Depressed Classes Conference at Yeola on 13 October 1935, so both statements are correct.

s: What is Ambedkar's reinterpretation of Buddhism known as?
x: Ambedkar's reinterpretation of Buddhism is called Navayana, meaning Neo-Buddhism. It gave rise to the Dalit Buddhist Movement.

s: According to the Supreme Court ruling of 24 March 2026, conversion out of which of the following religions results in the immediate loss of Scheduled Caste status under Clause 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950?
x: The ruling held that conversion out of Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism leads to immediate loss of Scheduled Caste status under Clause 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950.

s: Who supported Ambedkar's idea of considering Sikhism as an alternative to Hinduism?
x: B.S. Moonje supported the idea, while Gandhi, Rajagopalachari and Malaviya opposed it.

s: Which of the following pairs regarding Ambedkar's conversion to Buddhism is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Followers who accompanied him – about fifty thousand
x: About five lakh followers, mostly Mahars, accompanied him, not fifty thousand; the other pairs are correct.

s: On which date did Ambedkar embrace Buddhism?
x: He converted on 14 October 1956 at Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur; 13 October 1935 was only the Yeola declaration.

s: Where did Ambedkar embrace Buddhism in 1956?
x: The conversion took place at Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur; Yeola was the place of the 1935 declaration and he died in Delhi.

s: How many vows did Ambedkar administer at his conversion to Buddhism?
x: Ambedkar prescribed 22 vows at the 1956 conversion.

s:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's conversion to Buddhism:
1. About 5 lakh followers converted with him.
2. Most of the followers were Mahars.
3. The conversion took place in 1935.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: About 5 lakh followers, mostly Mahars, converted with him in 1956; 1935 was only the Yeola declaration.

s: In which year were Buddhists brought under the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950?
x: Sikhs were added in 1956 and Buddhists in 1990.

s: On which date did B.R. Ambedkar die?
x: Ambedkar died in Delhi on 6 December 1956, less than two months after his conversion at Nagpur.

s: Which of the following does Ambedkar's Navayana (Neo-Buddhism) reject?
x: Navayana rejects Karma, rebirth, monasticism, meditation and the four noble truths, and gives a rational, social reading of Buddhism.

s: In which year were Sikhs added to the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950?
x: Sikhs were added to the SC Order in 1956; Buddhists were added in 1990.

s: What was Ambedkar's critique of caste in Annihilation of Caste?
o: Only untouchability needed to be removed while the caste system could remain.
Caste had no connection with religious texts and could be reformed through charity alone.
The caste system as a whole had to be destroyed because it possessed religious sanction in the Shastras and Vedas.
Caste was an ideal division of labour that required only greater efficiency.
x: Ambedkar argued that caste had religious sanction in the Shastras and Vedas and that reform limited to untouchability was inadequate; the entire caste system had to go.

s: Who described caste as “not just a division of labour, but a division of labourers”?
x: The statement that caste is a division of labourers, rather than merely a division of labour, was made by B.R. Ambedkar.

s: What was Ambedkar's position regarding political power for the Depressed Classes?
o: Political power was necessary to protect their interests.
Political power could be secured only through religious conversion.
Political power should remain exclusively with caste Hindus.
Political power was irrelevant because social reform alone was sufficient.
x: Ambedkar held that political power was necessary for the Depressed Classes to protect themselves and secure their rights.

s: For which organisation was Ambedkar's Annihilation of Caste (1936) prepared as an address?
x: It was an undelivered address for the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal, Lahore; the session was cancelled and Ambedkar published it himself.

s: In Annihilation of Caste, Ambedkar called which of the following the "real remedy" for caste?
x: Ambedkar held inter-caste marriage to be the real remedy; change of heart and temple entry were Gandhi's methods.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Annihilation of Caste (1936)?
o: It held that caste has sanction in the Shastras and Vedas
It argued that the whole caste system must go
Gandhi replied to it in Harijan
It was delivered by Ambedkar at Lahore
x: The address was never delivered: the session was cancelled and Ambedkar published it himself.

s: Ambedkar later felt that the Poona Pact made the Dalits:
o: independent of caste Hindus in political matters
x: Ambedkar later felt the Pact made Dalits dependent on caste Hindus, although he had accepted joint electorates during the negotiations.

s: What was a major criticism made by Ambedkar against the Indian National Congress?
o: It opposed all constitutional safeguards for minorities.
It supported separate electorates for the Scheduled Castes.
It refused to treat caste as a political issue.
It treated caste exclusively as an economic issue.
x: Ambedkar criticised Congress for refusing to recognise caste as a political issue. His work What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables was published in 1945.

s: Under the Poona Pact (1932), how many seats were reserved for the Depressed Classes?
x:
Most books (NextGen, PMF, NCERT): 148 seats. Spectrum p.424 gives 147.
The Poona Pact raised the depressed classes' reserved seats in provincial legislatures from 71 to 148.

s: According to Ambedkar's Who Were the Shudras?, who were the Shudras originally?
o: A Kshatriya community degraded after conflict with Brahmins
An occupational group created by British legislation
A group formed exclusively from foreign invaders
x: Ambedkar argued that the Shudras were originally Kshatriyas who were degraded after conflict with Brahmins, who denied them the upanayana.

s: Which work of Ambedkar advanced the “broken men” theory regarding the origin of untouchability?
o: What Congress and Gandhi Have Done to the Untouchables
x: The Untouchables, published in 1948, dealt with the origin of untouchability and advanced the theory of “broken men.”

s:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's works:
1. Who Were the Shudras? was published in 1946.
2. The Untouchables was published in 1948.
3. The Buddha and His Dhamma was published in Ambedkar's lifetime.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Who Were the Shudras? appeared in 1946 and The Untouchables in 1948; The Buddha and His Dhamma was published posthumously in 1957.

s: On behalf of which organisation was States and Minorities submitted to the Constituent Assembly in 1947?
x: States and Minorities was a 1947 memorandum submitted to the Constituent Assembly on behalf of the Scheduled Castes Federation.

s: Which work of Ambedkar, published posthumously in 1957, became the basis of Navayana?
x: The Buddha and His Dhamma (1957, posthumous) gave a rational, social reading of Buddhism that became the basis of Navayana.

s: In which work did Ambedkar set out his proposals for State socialism?
x: States and Minorities proposed State ownership of key industries and agricultural land and nationalised insurance.

s: On which of the following did Gandhi and Ambedkar differ fundamentally?
o: Whether the whole caste system should be annihilated
x: Both sought uplift of the marginalised and stressed education, but differed on whether the whole caste system should be annihilated.

s: On which date did Ambedkar call the Indian village 'a sink of localism, a den of ignorance, narrow-mindedness and communalism' in the Constituent Assembly?
x: He said this on 4 November 1948, preferring the individual, not the village, as the basic unit.

s: Why did Ambedkar propose that State socialism should be written into the Constitution?
o: To ensure that a legislative majority could not undo it
To place economic policy exclusively under local bodies
To permit every village to frame a separate economic constitution
To prevent all state ownership of industries
x: Ambedkar wanted State socialism entrenched in the Constitution so that a temporary legislative majority could not reverse it.

s:
Consider the following statements about Ambedkar's proposals in States and Minorities (1947):
1. State ownership of agricultural land.
2. Nationalised insurance.
3. State socialism to be left to ordinary legislation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: He proposed State ownership of key industries and agricultural land and nationalised insurance, to be written into the Constitution so that a legislative majority could not undo them.

s: Rejecting Gandhi's Gram Swaraj and trusteeship, what did Ambedkar advocate?
x: Ambedkar rejected Gram Swaraj and trusteeship, favouring a strong, centralised constitutional democracy to protect minorities.

s: According to Ambedkar, what should be the basic unit of the Indian polity?
x: Ambedkar made the individual, not the village, the basic unit and called the village a sink of localism.

s: Who used the term 'Harijan' for the depressed classes?
x: Gandhi used the term 'Harijan'; Ambedkar rejected it in favour of Dalit/Scheduled Castes.

s:
Consider the following statements about separate electorates in 1932:
1. Gandhi opposed separate electorates for the Depressed Classes.
2. Ambedkar demanded separate electorates but settled for reserved seats under the Poona Pact.
Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
x: Gandhi opposed separate electorates and fasted in 1932; Ambedkar demanded them but ultimately settled for reserved seats under the Poona Pact.

s: The stalling of which of the following led to Ambedkar's resignation in 1951?
o: Constitution of the Scheduled Castes Federation
x: Ambedkar resigned in 1951 when the Hindu Code Bill, which dealt with inheritance, marriage and divorce, stalled.

s: In which year did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar found the Independent Labour Party?
x: He founded the ILP in 1936 and was Labour Member during 1942-46.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Resignation over the Hindu Code Bill – 1948
x: Ambedkar resigned in 1951 when the Hindu Code Bill stalled; the other pairs are correct.

s: As Labour Member (1942-46), which measure did Ambedkar back?
x: As Labour Member during 1942-46 Ambedkar backed the 8-hour working day; the others were his reform and State socialism proposals, not labour measures.

s: Which educational body did B.R. Ambedkar found in 1945?
x: Ambedkar founded the People's Education Society in 1945; it started Siddharth College in 1946.

s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar suggested which city as a second capital of India?
x: Ambedkar suggested Hyderabad as a second capital; he also proposed dividing Maharashtra and warned against huge states.

s: What was Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's position on the relationship between language and states?
o: He accepted “one state, one language” but not “one language, one state”.
He supported “one language, one state” but rejected “one state, one language”.
He supported both “one state, one language” and “one language, one state”.
He rejected both linguistic principles in favour of administrative states.
x: Ambedkar accepted the principle of one state, one language, but did not accept the principle of one language, one state.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Ambedkar's Thoughts on Linguistic States (1955)?
o: It proposed Hyderabad as a second capital
It suggested dividing UP, Bihar and MP
x: Ambedkar accepted 'one state, one language', not 'one language, one state'.
